title: Replacing exit() calls with function returns
description: Take some of the individual exit() calls and replace them with just returning out of a function, even main().

notes.body: I would like to understand why exit was used in the first place. This seems too obvious, perhaps.

Me too ;) Best I can come up with was one bad mistake that was copy/pasted many times.  I have several more commits lined up, but was using these patches to test how multiple commits that shouldn't be squashed works in gitlab.  I was trying to put in commits that didn't depend on !19662, but it looks like I failed.
All of this came from falling down a rabbit hole of #20432 and seeing the taps shouldn't be using exit()

commits_data.message:
Add return for commandline_early_options() to allow cleaner "exit"

Replace exit() calls in commandline_early_options() with return value so that applications to end abruptly

commits_data.title: Refactor commandline arg helpers to not exit on failure
commits_data.message:
Refactor commandline arg helpers to not exit on failure

Have the clopts_common helpers return success/fail (true/false) and have the desired return value passed in as an argument.  This allows failures to be handled by the calling applications and have a "cleaner" exit on failure.

commits_data.message:
Remove exit() from ui + cli taps

More graceful exits can be done by returning values or ignoring invalid data.

Also, just return TAP_PACKET_FAILED when LOAD() function is configured incorrectly and not exit()
